bull_bear.body:
- Dominant automotive glass position - approximately 80% share of the Indian passenger car glass segment, held with a healthy new-business win ratio
- Vertical integration from float glass manufacture through downstream value-added processing, strengthened by the third float plant at Soniyana
- Deep Localisation / 'QJCI' (Quality of Japan, Cost of India) model combining AGC group technology with Indian cost structures and in-house product design
- Proximity manufacturing: 15 plants and 11 sub-assembly units-cum-warehouses located near automotive and real-estate markets enabling just-in-time delivery, including an on-site assembly facility inside the Maruti Suzuki Kharkhoda campus
- Distribution reach in architectural glass through more than 1,424 stockists across India
- Consumer-facing service network - AIS Windshield Experts present in 79+ cities with 151+ dealerships, a 'Repair First' model, cashless insurance tie-ups and a written one-year workmanship warranty
- Engineering capability to design, develop and commission new products, process equipment, tools and fixtures for end-to-end manufacture of value-added automotive products
- OEM recognition - performance, quality, delivery and localisation awards from Maruti Suzuki, Honda Cars, Nissan, Uno Minda, Sandhar Technologies and Ashok Leyland during the year
- Circularity as a cost lever - recycled cullet forms 25-30% of glass input by value, reducing virgin raw-material and fuel use
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-activity concentration - the entire business is glass — The Board confirms there was no change in the nature of business during the year, and the reporting boundary covers only the Auto Glass, Architectural Glass and Consumer Glass SBUs. With no non-glass activity, a downturn in glass demand or glass economics has no offset elsewhere in the portfolio.
- Customer-segment concentration in automotive and construction end-markets — The Directors' Report attributes the year's satisfactory performance directly to improved demand in both the automotive and architectural segments, so earnings are levered to two cyclical end-markets and to the OEM customers behind them.
- Domestic-market concentration with negligible export diversification — The reporting scope covers pan-India operations only, with manufacturing, processing and warehousing sites concentrated in India. There is no overseas manufacturing base to buffer a domestic demand or policy shock.
- Forward-looking statement risk acknowledged by the Board — The Board's Statement of Responsibility states that the Report contains forward-looking statements based on current assumptions, industry conditions and the Company's strategic plans, which are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual outcomes to differ materially, and that AIS undertakes no obligation to update them.
- Group restructuring and integration execution risk — Three downstream subsidiaries (AIS Adhesives, AIS Distribution Services and GX Glass Sales & Services) were amalgamated into AIS Glass Solutions Limited under an NCLT-approved composite Scheme of Arrangement effective 1st July, 2025, and the transferee was renamed AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited. Consolidating several operating entities into one carries integration and execution exposure.
- Emergence of a material subsidiary shifting exposure below the listed entity — The Company had no material subsidiary in FY 2025-26, but AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited has been identified as a material subsidiary during FY 2026-27 on the basis of its financial statements. A growing share of value will sit in an entity whose results are not visible in the standalone accounts.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: AIS manufactures and processes glass across three Strategic Business Units - Automotive Glass, Architectural (Building & Construction) Glass and Consumer Glass. It runs an integrated network of float glass plants, automotive glass processing facilities, architectural glass processing units and sub-assembly locations across India, supplying laminated windshields, tempered sidelites and backlites, sunroofs and encapsulated glazing to domestic and global OEMs, and float, coated, reflective, mirror, insulated, security and acoustic glass to the architectural market. Through its Consumer Glass SBU it sells directly to retail customers via the AIS Windows, AIS Glasxperts and AIS Windshield Experts brands.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Automotive Glass:** Windshields, Sidelites, Backlites, Panoramic sunroof, Encapsulated quarter glasses, ADAS-ready windshields, Acoustic (NVH attenuation) glass, UV protection glass, IR heat rejection glass, Heating and defogging systems, White goods glass (refrigerator shelves and doors, washing machine lids)
- **Architectural Glass:** Float glass, Clear, tinted, reflective and mirror glass, Back painted and frosted glass, Energy-efficient coated / Low-E glass, Insulated glazing units, Lacquered glass, Security and acoustic glass, Fire-resistant glass, AIS Stronglas (impact resistance glass), AIS Securityglas (burglar resistant glass), AIS Acousticglas Shield (sound resistant glass), AIS Valuglas, AIS Securityplus, AIS Insulated-Glazed Unit, AIS Heat-Strengthened Glass, AIS Krystal (branded frosted glass), AIS Disegno, AIS Mesh Laminated, AIS Colored Laminated, AIS Fabric Laminated Glass, AIS Ceramic Frit, AIS Printed Glass, AIS Acid Etched Glass, AIS Swytchglas (privacy glass), AIS Integrated Blinds, AIS Pyrobel (fire resistant glass), Ecosense range (Ecosense Spectra, Ecosense Spring Plus, Ecosense Edge Natura, Ecosense Enhance), OPAL Trendz range (Petal Delight, Nova Craft)
- **Consumer Glass:** AIS Windows (uPVC and aluminium doors and windows), AIS Glasxperts (glass lifestyle solutions - doors, windows, staircases, balustrades, canopies, pool enclosures), AIS Windshield Experts (automotive glass repair and replacement), Energy-efficient IGUs, Solar-control and Low-E glass, Safety and toughened glass, Facades, partitions and skylights

outlook.body:
- Value-addition as the core lever: pursue superior value-added products, more efficient assets, sharper market segmentation and reliable service rather than relying on external trade remedies - value addition is a stated core strategic aim and a direct lever for margin improvement in architectural glass
- Deep Localisation under the 'QJCI' (Quality of Japan, Cost of India) philosophy - designing products in-house for Indian climatic and customer conditions and localising manufacturing capacity to reduce import dependence
- Shift the operating priority from building capacity to absorbing it: stabilise commissioned assets and improve the returns generated on the recent investment cycle, with operational excellence and financial prudence
- Build a direct-to-consumer platform through AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited, formed by merging the downstream businesses (ADSL, AIA and GX) into one entity to rationalise expenses and sharpen D2C focus
- Deepen OEM co-creation for advanced automotive glazing - solar/UV coatings, acoustic glass, ADAS-ready windshields, panoramic and lightweight laminated solutions - to raise glass content per vehicle in EVs and premium ICE models
- Expand premium architectural glass offerings (solar-control coatings, neutral/high-transmission glass, tailored laminates) and strengthen partnerships with window and system integrators and large builders
- Accelerate R&D on energy-efficient and eco-friendly glass (low-iron, Low-E, vacuum insulated, dynamic smart glazing) to serve green building compliance
- Expand renewable energy and cogeneration to secure low-cost power, and raise circularity through higher cullet rates in furnaces
- Build agile procurement and hedging policies to manage raw material and energy price volatility
- Engage with trade bodies to shape standards and import policies that sustain fair competition
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: AIS describes FY 2025-26 as the closing year of the largest investment cycle in its history, with capital expenditure of Rs 666.26 crores during the year. The cycle comprised the third float-glass plant at Soniyana (Rajasthan), a float line cold repair at Roorkee, the Phase 2 expansion at Patan, and the on-site assembly facility at Kharkhoda, which together added significant capacity and capability. The new Soniyana float glass plant was commissioned during the year and, together with the Roorkee refurbishment, is expected to add to overall financial performance from next year; the Soniyana commencement strengthened vertical integration, localisation, inventory optimisation and supply-chain resilience. Brownfield investment continued at Patan, Chennai and Bawal, with Patan Phase 3 work started and Phase 4 implementation initiated - a phased approach that aligns capacity expansion with demand, technology and productivity requirements. Assembly operations at Nashik (Maharashtra) were expanded and ASN-Nashik was commissioned in FY 2025-26. Management characterises FY 2025-26 as a year of transition from building capacity to absorbing capacity, from commissioning assets to stabilising them, and from undertaking capital expenditure to improving the returns generated by it. Funding was supported by a Rs 1,000.00 crores QIP completed in 2025, the third capital raise in AIS's history, while total debt was reduced to Rs 2,058.67 crores with debt-equity improving from 0.96x to 0.52x. Separately, the downstream businesses ADSL, AIA and GX were merged into AIS Glass Solutions Limited, subsequently renamed AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited, consolidating the consumer-facing entities.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Improved demand in both automotive and architectural segments made FY 2025-26 a satisfactory year, with financial and operational performance largely close to budgets
- Indian vehicle production increased to 3.47 crore units in FY 2025-26 from 3.10 crore units in FY 2024-25, making India the third largest producer globally, with robust domestic demand supported by low finance rates and rising incomes
- Rapid electrification: registrations of electric passenger vehicles rose approximately 80% in FY 2025-26, supported by FAME policies and expanding charging infrastructure; EVs and premium ICE models demand lightweight laminated and panoramic glazing, increasing content per vehicle
- Connected and safety features (ADAS, HUDs, cameras) becoming standard means windshields must integrate solar-control coatings, acoustic layers, HUD compatibility and sensors - shifting glass from commodity to value-add
- Urbanisation, infrastructure investment and expansion of organised real estate are driving construction demand; India's real estate sector is expected to reach US$5.8 trillion by 2047 and US$1 trillion by 2030
- Green building codes and certification frameworks (IGBC, GRIHA) are making high-performance glass a standard requirement rather than a niche - IGBC has registered over 19,820 projects covering more than 16.20 billion sq.ft
- Homeowners, architects and developers increasingly seek higher value-added glass for daylight, heat management, acoustics, safety, privacy and visual quality as energy-efficiency standards tighten
- Countervailing pressure in architectural glass: additional domestic capacity plus aggressively priced cheaper imports from Chinese transplants in south-east Asian countries continued to pressure the domestic float glass industry, partially offset by a Minimum Import Price (MIP) imposed on clear float glass
- Investments in the new Soniyana float plant and the Roorkee float line refurbishment are expected to add to overall financial performance from next year
- Glass production is energy- and raw-material-intensive; silica, soda ash, gas and power costs directly impact margins, and commodity price swings remain a risk even as renewables gradually lower power costs
- Government policy support - Make in India, PLI schemes (which had attracted about Rs 2.16 lakh crore of committed investments by 2025), infrastructure budgets and rising localisation targets - improves demand visibility and rewards local value addition
- Consumer Glass is deliberately being grown slowly to understand consumer requirements and build B2C processes, with management optimistic about exponential growth of AIS-CG thereafter

risks.risk: Single-activity concentration - the entire business is glass
risks.note: The Board confirms there was no change in the nature of business during the year, and the reporting boundary covers only the Auto Glass, Architectural Glass and Consumer Glass SBUs. With no non-glass activity, a downturn in glass demand or glass economics has no offset elsewhere in the portfolio.

risks.risk: Customer-segment concentration in automotive and construction end-markets
risks.note: The Directors' Report attributes the year's satisfactory performance directly to improved demand in both the automotive and architectural segments, so earnings are levered to two cyclical end-markets and to the OEM customers behind them.

risks.risk: Domestic-market concentration with negligible export diversification
risks.note: The reporting scope covers pan-India operations only, with manufacturing, processing and warehousing sites concentrated in India. There is no overseas manufacturing base to buffer a domestic demand or policy shock.

risks.risk: Forward-looking statement risk acknowledged by the Board
risks.note: The Board's Statement of Responsibility states that the Report contains forward-looking statements based on current assumptions, industry conditions and the Company's strategic plans, which are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual outcomes to differ materially, and that AIS undertakes no obligation to update them.

risks.risk: Group restructuring and integration execution risk
risks.note: Three downstream subsidiaries (AIS Adhesives, AIS Distribution Services and GX Glass Sales & Services) were amalgamated into AIS Glass Solutions Limited under an NCLT-approved composite Scheme of Arrangement effective 1st July, 2025, and the transferee was renamed AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited. Consolidating several operating entities into one carries integration and execution exposure.

risks.risk: Emergence of a material subsidiary shifting exposure below the listed entity
risks.note: The Company had no material subsidiary in FY 2025-26, but AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited has been identified as a material subsidiary during FY 2026-27 on the basis of its financial statements. A growing share of value will sit in an entity whose results are not visible in the standalone accounts.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Improved demand in both automotive and architectural segments made FY 2025-26 a satisfactory year, with financial and operational performance largely close to budgets
- Indian vehicle production increased to 3.47 crore units in FY 2025-26 from 3.10 crore units in FY 2024-25, making India the third largest producer globally, with robust domestic demand supported by low finance rates and rising incomes
- Rapid electrification: registrations of electric passenger vehicles rose approximately 80% in FY 2025-26, supported by FAME policies and expanding charging infrastructure; EVs and premium ICE models demand lightweight laminated and panoramic glazing, increasing content per vehicle
- Connected and safety features (ADAS, HUDs, cameras) becoming standard means windshields must integrate solar-control coatings, acoustic layers, HUD compatibility and sensors - shifting glass from commodity to value-add
- Urbanisation, infrastructure investment and expansion of organised real estate are driving construction demand; India's real estate sector is expected to reach US$5.8 trillion by 2047 and US$1 trillion by 2030
- Green building codes and certification frameworks (IGBC, GRIHA) are making high-performance glass a standard requirement rather than a niche - IGBC has registered over 19,820 projects covering more than 16.20 billion sq.ft
- Homeowners, architects and developers increasingly seek higher value-added glass for daylight, heat management, acoustics, safety, privacy and visual quality as energy-efficiency standards tighten
- Countervailing pressure in architectural glass: additional domestic capacity plus aggressively priced cheaper imports from Chinese transplants in south-east Asian countries continued to pressure the domestic float glass industry, partially offset by a Minimum Import Price (MIP) imposed on clear float glass
- Investments in the new Soniyana float plant and the Roorkee float line refurbishment are expected to add to overall financial performance from next year
- Glass production is energy- and raw-material-intensive; silica, soda ash, gas and power costs directly impact margins, and commodity price swings remain a risk even as renewables gradually lower power costs
- Government policy support - Make in India, PLI schemes (which had attracted about Rs 2.16 lakh crore of committed investments by 2025), infrastructure budgets and rising localisation targets - improves demand visibility and rewards local value addition
- Consumer Glass is deliberately being grown slowly to understand consumer requirements and build B2C processes, with management optimistic about exponential growth of AIS-CG thereafter

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Value-addition as the core lever: pursue superior value-added products, more efficient assets, sharper market segmentation and reliable service rather than relying on external trade remedies - value addition is a stated core strategic aim and a direct lever for margin improvement in architectural glass
- Deep Localisation under the 'QJCI' (Quality of Japan, Cost of India) philosophy - designing products in-house for Indian climatic and customer conditions and localising manufacturing capacity to reduce import dependence
- Shift the operating priority from building capacity to absorbing it: stabilise commissioned assets and improve the returns generated on the recent investment cycle, with operational excellence and financial prudence
- Build a direct-to-consumer platform through AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited, formed by merging the downstream businesses (ADSL, AIA and GX) into one entity to rationalise expenses and sharpen D2C focus
- Deepen OEM co-creation for advanced automotive glazing - solar/UV coatings, acoustic glass, ADAS-ready windshields, panoramic and lightweight laminated solutions - to raise glass content per vehicle in EVs and premium ICE models
- Expand premium architectural glass offerings (solar-control coatings, neutral/high-transmission glass, tailored laminates) and strengthen partnerships with window and system integrators and large builders
- Accelerate R&D on energy-efficient and eco-friendly glass (low-iron, Low-E, vacuum insulated, dynamic smart glazing) to serve green building compliance
- Expand renewable energy and cogeneration to secure low-cost power, and raise circularity through higher cullet rates in furnaces
- Build agile procurement and hedging policies to manage raw material and energy price volatility
- Engage with trade bodies to shape standards and import policies that sustain fair competition

Brownfield investment continued at Patan, Chennai and Bawal, with Patan Phase 3 work started and Phase 4 implementation initiated - a phased approach that aligns capacity expansion with demand, technology and productivity requirements. - Engineering capability to design, develop and commission new products, process equipment, tools and fixtures for end-to-end manufacture of value-added automotive products
- OEM recognition - performance, quality, delivery and localisation awards from Maruti Suzuki, Honda Cars, Nissan, Uno Minda, Sandhar Technologies and Ashok Leyland during the year
- Circularity as a cost lever - recycled cullet forms 25-30% of glass input by value, reducing virgin raw-material and fuel use

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Single-activity concentration - the entire business is glass — The Board confirms there was no change in the nature of business during the year, and the reporting boundary covers only the Auto Glass, Architectural Glass and Consumer Glass SBUs. With no non-glass activity, a downturn in glass demand or glass economics has no offset elsewhere in the portfolio.
- Customer-segment concentration in automotive and construction end-markets — The Directors' Report attributes the year's satisfactory performance directly to improved demand in both the automotive and architectural segments, so earnings are levered to two cyclical end-markets and to the OEM customers behind them.
- Domestic-market concentration with negligible export diversification — The reporting scope covers pan-India operations only, with manufacturing, processing and warehousing sites concentrated in India. There is no overseas manufacturing base to buffer a domestic demand or policy shock.
- Forward-looking statement risk acknowledged by the Board — The Board's Statement of Responsibility states that the Report contains forward-looking statements based on current assumptions, industry conditions and the Company's strategic plans, which are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual outcomes to differ materially, and that AIS undertakes no obligation to update them.
- Group restructuring and integration execution risk — Three downstream subsidiaries (AIS Adhesives, AIS Distribution Services and GX Glass Sales & Services) were amalgamated into AIS Glass Solutions Limited under an NCLT-approved composite Scheme of Arrangement effective 1st July, 2025, and the transferee was renamed AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited. Consolidating several operating entities into one carries integration and execution exposure.
- Emergence of a material subsidiary shifting exposure below the listed entity — The Company had no material subsidiary in FY 2025-26, but AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited has been identified as a material subsidiary during FY 2026-27 on the basis of its financial statements. A growing share of value will sit in an entity whose results are not visible in the standalone accounts.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Value-addition as the core lever: pursue superior value-added products, more efficient assets, sharper market segmentation and reliable service rather than relying on external trade remedies - value addition is a stated core strategic aim and a direct lever for margin improvement in architectural glass
- Deep Localisation under the 'QJCI' (Quality of Japan, Cost of India) philosophy - designing products in-house for Indian climatic and customer conditions and localising manufacturing capacity to reduce import dependence
